findings.explanation: The Splunk Universal Forwarder is downloaded from splunk.com, not Splunkbase, and it has no SNMP polling input; splunkbase.splunk.com/app/617 returns 404. A reader following this would not collect any UPS data.
findings.quote: Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll
findings.suggested_fix: Name the actual SNMP collector: Splunk Connect for SNMP or the SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase 1537), polling PowerNet-MIB upsAdvInputLineVoltage. Drop the Universal Forwarder and the 617 ID.

findings.explanation: SC4SNMP writes polling events as sourcetype sc4snmp:event to index netops by default, but the spl expects sourcetype snmp:apc:ups in index=power with a flat ups_name field. Nothing explains the override or extraction. The repository guide uses sourcetype snmp:ups.
findings.quote: Splunk Connect for SNMP (SC4SNMP) or SNMP Modular Input
findings.suggested_fix: Document how sourcetype snmp:apc:ups, index=power and ups_name are produced (SC4SNMP sourcetypePollingEvents/eventIndex overrides plus props), or align with the guide's snmp:ups sourcetype.

findings.explanation: The SPL defaults nominal_input_voltage to 230, so every 120 V or 208 V UPS deviates far more than 8% and alerts on every sample. The implementation never says where nominal_input_voltage comes from; it is not a PowerNet-MIB object.
findings.quote: (1) Normalize nominal voltage per region. (2) Correlate with ATS transfers.
findings.suggested_fix: Tell the reader to populate nominal_input_voltage per UPS from a lookup (asset inventory or the UPS nameplate input rating) before scheduling. Warn that the 230 V fallback only fits 230 V sites, and name the ATS UC (UC-15.4.8) for the correlation step.

findings.explanation: This lists title words in place of an explanation. It never says the search flags 5-minute samples where input voltage deviates more than 8% from nominal, either high or low.
findings.quote: Keywords: APC, UPS, SNMP, Input, Voltage. Focuses on Brownout Detection behaviour
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the detection: per-UPS input line voltage compared with the site nominal, with rows where the absolute deviation exceeds 8% (sags/brownouts or surges) charted every 5 minutes.

findings.explanation: These are generic REST/HEC troubleshooting steps that don't apply to SNMP polling of a UPS network management card, and the 'joins/lookups enrich owner' text describes SPL that does not exist.
findings.quote: Enable the modular input or HEC token ... unless the vendor API rate-limits lower ... inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite for SNMP: SNMPv3 credentials on the NMC, UDP 161 reachability, poll interval, PowerNet-MIB loading, the nominal-voltage lookup, and SNMP timeout errors in the collector logs.

findings.explanation: These are template scenarios that don't describe a real cause of voltage deviation alerts.
findings.quote: Batch `avg` on `snmp:apc:ups` — Scheduled automation elevates `vin` without crossing `pct_dev` > 8
findings.suggested_fix: List real causes: wrong or missing nominal voltage for the site (the most common one), generator testing or utility switching during planned transfers, a single bad SNMP sample (0 V read during an NMC reboot), and sites with known wide utility tolerance.

findings.explanation: The collection path is wrong and the hardcoded 230 V nominal would alert constantly at 120/208 V sites, so the UC cannot have been validated as written.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft or unverified until an SME validates it against real UPS data.

findings.explanation: There is no field named activity in the SPL or the data.
findings.suggested_fix: Say the UC tracks UPS input line voltage against nominal.

findings.explanation: A PDU product-category page is cited for a UPS input-voltage UC, and the SC4SNMP link points to a Splunkbase search although SC4SNMP is not distributed there.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the PowerNet-MIB upsAdvInputLineVoltage definition and the SC4SNMP docs (https://splunk.github.io/splunk-connect-for-snmp/).

findings.explanation: The detection uses polled values, not traps.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove snmp_trap or add a trap-based variant (for example, APC input-voltage traps).

firewalled_field_flags.issue: nominal_input_voltage is not a PowerNet-MIB or RFC 1628 object and defaults to 230, so 120 V/208 V UPSes always exceed 8% and alert continuously. The nominal should come from a lookup keyed on ups_name. Because of the where clause, the timechart only plots deviant samples, so the 'Timechart input V' visualization will show gaps rather than the voltage trend.

summary: The input-voltage deviation search uses real MIB objects (APC upsAdvInputLineVoltage, RFC 1628 upsInputVoltage), but it hardcodes a 230 V nominal and the surrounding text is template residue. The collection path names the Universal Forwarder as a Splunkbase SNMP input, which is wrong.
